Replaced the OEM unit with this one.  Also replaced the board and the evap fan as part of trying to stop the ice from melting during defrost and refreezing.  We had also experienced periods when the unit stopped cooling and had to be reset (the board was bad). The OEM defrost was not bad, but I thought I would replace it as part of the repairs.  After all the parts were replaced the unit ran great, for a few days.  Then the ice started to melt even worse than before.  After research I determined that the thermister was most likely bad so I ordered two supposedly OEM parts to replace both of the parts in the freezer.  I was VERY surprised when I opened the panel to find the defrost element along with the wires and parts of the inner wall melted!  Obviously this this thing had been way too hot (hence the melting ice). (note: during the troubleshooting of the issue, I had tested the overlimit thermostat and it broke the circuit at approx 180' which was actually lower than the OEM part I pulled out. Specs call for 140') I tested the upper thermister and found it was bad (read 12k ohms at room temp, the new ones were 5.86k ohms).  This one controls the defrost temp. It would appear that the thermister that came with this kit had failed or was bad originally. (I did not test it before installation)  Fortunately I still had the OEM defrost heater and replaced the bad connectors then put the original defrost back in (after I tested it) along with the new thermisters. This kit includes a heater, thermister and thermostat supposedly to repair a GE Refrigerator among others.  I've experimented carefully with all 3 items received in this kit.  Heater:  Works fine, had it for about 6 months now.  Thermister: Not in spec.  The correct OHM reading should be 16 OHM at 32 deg F for a GE fridge.  The one in this kit measured 24 OHM at 32 deg F.  This will not work, it causes fridge to think it's much colder than it really is causing the fridge temp to be way to warm.  Thermostat: Garbage.  It's supposed to open up at about 40 deg F and above (i.e. create open circuit).  The one in this kit stays closed all the time.  I connected a meter to it and soaked it in hot water (about 80 + deg F) for 10 minutes and it never opened up.  This is dangerous because the thermostat is supposed to prevent the heater from overheating the freezer compartment.  I'm not sure if I happen to receive defective parts or if they are all defective.  Either way, 2 out of 3 bad parts is not a good sign.

This was a good replacement for the defrost heater. My old one might actually have been OK because I found when replacing that the wire spade connections were corroded with surface rust from the wet environment, so I added high temp dielectric grease to protect going forward. But it works well.

The thermistor was WAY OFF CALIBRATION. You need to really really make sure that at 32F (ice water) the resistance is 16.3K. What I got in this product read 35K... since the thermistor determines when the defrost heater shuts off, the result was my defrost cycle would take the freezer compartment to 70F+, melting everything. Also, the thermistor needs to be mounted on the topmost pipe of the evaporator... top topmost. Lower (like where the thermostat is) results in reading too cold and again, overheating by a little.

The thermostat is really just an overtemp protection to shut off at 140F, in normal operation it does nothing. The unit provided in this kit is OK but has a less secure latching clip than the OEM part, which makes it more likely to fall off the evap pipe.

This defrost heater seemed to work fine at first, but after about a month we noticed that it was noticeably heating up our freezer! We noticed that our ice in the ice maker had been partially melted and refrozen into a solid mass and wouldn't dispense through the door receptacle. There was also some drips that had refrozen beneath our ice maker on the side and back walls. When we noticed this our freezer that was set for 0 degrees Fahrenheit was currently at 9 degrees... It was in the process of returning back to it's proper temperature. Later that evening we checked it again and noticed a weird overheated smell in the freezer (either from heated plastic or possibly from melted water) and pulled out the bottom bin to notice that there was a bright red glow coming from the defrost heater behind the back wall. We immediately unplugged the refrigerator, let the heater cool a bit, removed it and replugged the refrigerator without it until we could get the OEM part ordered and installed instead of this obviously flawed generic part. When we removed the heater, it had browned the edges of the positive and negative connector wires for it. Yikes! I'm so glad we happened to keep most of our food out of this freezer until we decided it was fully repaired. This replacement does not seem to have the longevity of the OEM heater given it's somewhat different materials (mine died in 9 months vs 7 years for the OEM). Consider a pricier real OEM part given that the heater operates in pretty hostile conditions, and will do about 0.5-3 defrost cycles per 24 hours.

But do not fear - the customer service for this particular offering is excellent. Don't hesitate to contact them in case you want a refund for this one so that you can buy the genuine one. I got a prompt refund upon request.

A pro tip here - if you are replacing the heater, just defrost the heater bracket itself, and install the new heater. Then turn on the fridge, enter the diagnostics mode by pushing the 4 temperature adjustment buttons at once (getting to the blinking 00 00 on the temperature panel), and toggle "1 4" mode to turn on the heater. The heater will light up. Wait for it to work and defrost the rest of the coil. To turn the heater off when done, toggle "1 4" mode again. Please see the attached images on how this works in practice. You also get an extra bonus, you get to see your new heater in action!

This part did not work like it should. After first defrost cycle, we noticed a burnt smell, and that smell absorbed into the ice. Every defrost cycle there was a burning smell and everything in the freezer starts to defrost, then freezes again. The ice starts to melt, then freeze, and turn into a block of ice and the auger can’t break it up. Decided to pull the back freezer cover off and found the problem....this part was only in the freezer for 3 days. It’s over heating, melting the element terminals, and over heating the inside of the freezer to the point that everything starts to defrost. There was nothing incorrect about the instal of this part. It just didn’t work for me. Good luck if you decide to buy this. It may work, it may not.
